Key audit matter:
Valuation of loan note measured at fair value
As described in notes 5 (d) and 24 of the
financial statements, the Group holds a
loan note which is measured at fair value.
To determine the fair value of the loan note,
management has used various market driven
approaches. Management also applied other
option valuation methods. The valuation
involves a significant degree of judgement
mainly in:
• The selection of the valuation method to
use and weights attributed to the selected
methods; and
• The selction of relevant market
comparators to the customer whose
facilities are being fair valued.
Changes in the valuation approach and the
underlying assumptions could result in material
variations in the carrying amount of the asset.
Accounting consideration of the Merger transaction
As disclosed in note 1 and note 46 of the
financial statements, the NCBA Group arose
from the merger of NIC Group PLC (NIC) and
Commercial Bank of Africa Limited (CBA) on 1
October 2019.
The accounting and financial reporting of
the merger transaction involved complex and
significant management judgments such as
• The identification of the accounting
acquirer in the transaction;
• The determination, measurement and
recognition of identifiable intangible
assets not previously recognised by the
merged entities and the assessment of
their useful lives; and
How our audit addressed the matter:
We performed the following procedures:
• In conjunction with our valuation experts,
we evaluated the appropriateness of the
valuation methods used by management and
the reasonableness of the values derived.
• We carried out a sensitivity analysis of the
fair value selected by applying different
assumptions and producing a range of values.
• We assessed the adequacy of the disclosure
of relating to the facility in the financial
statements in accordance with International
Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)
requirements.
• We obtained an understanding of the
transaction and in conjunction with our
accounting advisory team, assessed the
nature of the transaction and the accounting
implications;
• In conjunction with our valuation experts,
we evaluated the reasonableness of
management’s assumptions in the
determination and measurement of
identifiable intangible assets not previously
recognised by the merged entities and the
estimation of useful lives;
• We tested the determination of the fair value
of the consideration paid by the acquirer in
line with the transaction agreements and the
provisions of the financial reporting standards
